title: Ghost Poll Pads
subtitle: VoterTrack Compromise & Public Trust

brief.userPrompt: Thursday 10/29/2026, the fourth-to-last day of early voting for the 2026 general election in Lisle County. At 08:10 three voters at the Early Vote Center (18 South Market Street, Carrow) are shown on their Poll Pads as 'mail ballot issued' though they never asked for one; by 10:00 there are 23 such voters and a line out the door. Voter Registration Manager Beth Saylor finds that 1,186 records in Precinct 104, Precinct 105 and Precinct 207 were changed in VoterTrack (LCBOE-VR01) between 02:05 and 02:40 Wednesday by the account of Voter Registration Clerk Nina Ruiz, who on Tuesday clicked a 'Secretary of State directive update' email and approved a multi-factor prompt; her mailbox has a forwarding rule. At 11:30 poll workers for Polling Location 6 (Carrow Community Church, Precinct 111 and Precinct 112) receive an email from her account saying their location moved back to Carrow Middle School. At 13:00 a video viewed 200,000 times says Lisle County 'deleted 10,000 voters' and that the DS200 scanners are connected to the internet. Decisions: disabling the account and preserving the evidence, freezing record changes (COOP-DR-5), whether to hold the 10/31 final pollbook load and rebuild it from the statewide voter registration database, provisional ballots for affected voters, correcting the spoofed notice, reports to the Ohio Secretary of State, CISA and the FBI, the 22-month records hold, Board notification, and a public statement (COOP-DR-6) that tells voters how to check their registration without naming any party or candidate.
audience: Election-Day Operations (Voter Registration and Mail Ballots)
constraints: Every email address of the board and the county uses the exercise domain lislevotes.example; outside parties use fictional domains and fictional outlet names (Channel 9, The Carrow Courier); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (the Ohio Secretary of State's office, CISA, the FBI, vendors, the managed SOC, Board members, voters, reporters) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.
Never name a real candidate or political party, never depict a real election result, and keep every contest fictional (Carrow City Council District 1 to District 4, Measure A, Measure B).

overview.theme: Credential Theft, Data Tampering, and Rapid Public Communication
overview.threat: An attacker compromised the account of Voter Registration Clerk Nina Ruiz by impersonating the Ohio Secretary of State in a phishing email. The attacker used her credentials to alter 1,186 voter records in VoterTrack between 02:05 and 02:40 on Wednesday, 10/29/2026. The changes included falsely marking voters as having received mail ballots, enabling unauthorized edits to pollbook data, and enabling a forwarding rule to exfiltrate her inbox. The attacker then used her account to send a spoofed notice to poll workers at Polling Location 6 (Carrow Community Church), falsely claiming the location had moved back to Carrow Middle School. This incident impacts the integrity of the voter registration database, the accuracy of pollbooks, and the operational readiness of election staff across multiple polling locations and the Early Vote Center.
overview.operationalImpact: At the Early Vote Center (18 South Market Street, Carrow), 23 voters are falsely shown as having received mail ballots; poll workers are unable to verify eligibility and must manually process checks, creating a line out the door. At Polling Location 6 (Carrow Community Church), poll workers receive a spoofed email from Nina Ruiz’s account directing them to a non-existent location, causing confusion and delays. The results website (results.lislevotes.example) shows a degraded load due to corrupted data feeds from VoterTrack. The hotline (555-0140) receives 42 calls in 30 minutes from voters reporting they were 'wrongly issued' ballots. The Board website (lislevotes.example) shows a 'Voter Registration Update' banner, but the underlying data is compromised. The Election Operations Center is activated, and staff begin to detect anomalies in the status board. The public information team must respond to a viral video (200,000 views) falsely claiming 10,000 voters were deleted and that scanners are internet-connected.

overview.targetAudience: Command (Director and Deputy Director), Elections IT and County Security, Election-Day Operations (Voter Registration and Mail Ballots), Voting Systems, Security and Sheriff's Liaison, Public Information
overview.location: Lisle County Board of Elections, Carrow, Lisle County, Ohio

objectives.name: Credential Integrity
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to detect and isolate a compromised user account in VoterTrack by verifying login patterns, disabling access, and initiating forensic preservation of logs within 15 minutes of first anomaly report.

objectives.name: Pollbook Accuracy
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to validate and correct pollbook data for Polling Location 6 using a trusted, air-gapped copy of the VoterTrack export, ensuring no unauthorized changes are applied during the emergency load.

objectives.name: Public Trust Management
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to issue a unified public statement via the PIO that corrects a viral misinformation claim about voter deletion, using the EAC/CISA communications guide and citing verified data from the Voter Registration Manager.

objectives.name: System Containment
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to isolate the VoterTrack database from the network and block external data exfiltration by disabling the forwarding rule and revoking API access from the compromised account within 10 minutes of confirmation.

roles.name: Chief Election Official (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Manages activation of the contingency plan, polling location relocation, and public statements in coordination with counsel and the PIO.
standingOrders: Act First: if the Board's public statements and legal advice conflict, follow the Director's directive as Incident Commander.
Verify All: never accept a system status as final without cross-checking with the physical log or a second source.
Delegate Authority: if the Board is delayed, use COOP-DR-2 to move the Early Vote Center to the alternate site without waiting for full approval.
Report Up: immediately notify the Board and the Secretary of State's office upon confirming a Level 1 incident.

roles.name: Deputy Director (Election-Day Operations Center)
roles.description: Runs the election-day operations center, hotline, rovers, staffing and logistics, and maintains the incident log and status board.
standingOrders: Track All: maintain real-time updates on the status board for every polling location and the Early Vote Center.
Rover First: dispatch a rover to Polling Location 6 within 5 minutes of receiving a report of a location move.
Log All: record every call and message in LCBOE-F-07 and LCBOE-F-25, including rumors and voter complaints.
Coordinate All: ensure all teams report to the Operations Center every 15 minutes during a Level 2 or Level 1 incident.

roles.name: Elections IT Manager / County CISO
roles.description: Owns the network, email, identity, voter registration system access, results website, and isolation decisions.
standingOrders: Isolate Fast: if a user account is compromised, isolate the system and disable access within 5 minutes.
Preserve Logs: never delete or alter logs before forensic review; preserve all access and authentication records.
Report Out: immediately contact the managed SOC and CISA if external data exfiltration is detected.
No Trust: if a system shows a discrepancy between the field and the screen, trust the field (e.g., the paper pollbook) over the digital display.

roles.name: Voting Systems Manager
roles.description: Owns logic and accuracy testing, tabulator chain of custody, seals, and vendor escalation.
standingOrders: Chain of Custody: if any tabulator or media is moved or accessed during a cyber incident, document the event and notify the Director immediately.
Test All: never proceed with a tabulation without a verified, air-gapped logic and accuracy test.
Escalate Fast: if a vendor (e.g., ES&S) fails to respond within 30 minutes, contact the U.S. Election Assistance Commission directly.
Seal First: if any tamper-evident seal is broken or missing, halt all processing and report to the Director.

roles.name: Facility Security Manager / Sheriff's Election Liaison
roles.description: Owns warehouse access, ballot transport escorts, threats to staff, and protest response.
standingOrders: Secure All: if any facility shows signs of unauthorized access, secure the perimeter and contact the Sheriff's Office immediately.
Escort All: if a ballot transport is delayed or rerouted, ensure a two-person escort is in place at all times.
Report Threats: if a staff member reports a credible threat, immediately notify the Director and the Sheriff's Office.
No Solo: never allow a single individual to enter the count room or warehouse without a second person present.

roles.name: Communications Director (PIO)
roles.description: Owns voter information, rumor control, media messages, and the Board’s public narrative.
standingOrders: Speak Only: the PIO is the only authorized voice to the media; all messages must be cleared with the Director and counsel.
Fact First: every public message must state what is known, what voters should do, and where to get help; never speculate on responsibility.
Rumor Log: maintain LCBOE-F-25 and update it every 10 minutes during a Level 2 or Level 1 incident.
CISA First: if a cyber incident is confirmed, immediately reference the EAC/CISA Election Infrastructure Incident Response Communications Guide in all public statements.

phases.title: The Glitch
phases.goal: Test the team's ability to recognize and respond to ambiguous signs of compromise, particularly the reluctance to act on anomalous data from a trusted system, and to initiate basic forensic checks on a user account.
beats: At 08:12, a front-line poll worker at the Early Vote Center (18 South Market Street, Carrow) calls the hotline (555-0140) reporting that 23 voters in the queue are marked as 'Mail Ballot Received' in the system, but they have not requested one; the worker notes, 'This is not right — these people are here to vote in person.'

At 08:18, the IT team receives a SIEM alert from LCBOE-FS01 showing an unexpected outbound connection from the Microsoft 365 tenant to a foreign IP (104.213.142.77) via a non-standard port, but no associated user alert; the alert is logged as 'Low Priority' by the on-call engineer and not escalated.

At 08:25, the VoterTrack system logs show a series of rapid edits to 1,186 voter records in the 'Absentee Ballot Status' field, all timestamped between 02:05 and 02:40 on 10/29/2026; the edits were made from IP address 10.100.45.12, which is not in the county’s internal network range, and the user account 'nruiz@lislevotes.example' was used, which belongs to VR Clerk Nina Ruiz.

At 08:30, the mail ballot tracking service (linked to VoterTrack) sends a spoofed notice to poll workers at Polling Location 6 (Carrow Community Church), falsely stating that the location has reverted to Carrow Middle School (the old site), with a fake signature from 'Nina Ruiz' and a modified link to a non-existent web portal.

At 08:42, the Board website (lislevotes.example) displays a 'Voter Registration Update' banner with a headline that reads, 'Voters in Precincts 111 and 112 have been re-registered to a new location'; the underlying data is corrupted and not synchronized with the statewide database, but no one has yet questioned its accuracy.

phases.title: The Crisis
phases.goal: Test the team's ability to transition from reactive triage to unified command under pressure, recognize a critical public misinformation event, and force an official incident declaration based on operational disruption and external pressure.
beats: At 09:15, the results website (results.lislevotes.example) fails to load properly; the front-end displays a corrupted data feed showing 1,186 voters in Precinct 111 and 112 as having voted via mail, despite no ballots being issued; the page loads slowly and shows a 'Processing Error' on the dashboard.

At 09:22, the hotline (555-0140) receives 42 calls in 30 minutes from voters reporting they were 'wrongly issued' mail ballots; a local reporter from The Carrow Courier calls the PIO, stating, 'We’re getting 10,000 calls from people saying they were deleted from the voter rolls — is that true?'

At 09:30, the front-end of the results website is replaced by a fake error page that mimics a CISA alert, showing a fake 'Election Integrity Advisory' with a red banner and a link to a phishing domain (phish.cisa.gov.lislevotes.example); the page is visible to all users and not blocked by the web filter.

At 09:38, the County CISO (Trent Gallagher) confirms that the forwarding rule on Nina Ruiz’s Microsoft 365 account has been activated, routing all incoming emails to an external address (nruiz@phishmail.net), and that the account has made 120 API calls to the VoterTrack database between 02:05 and 02:40 — all from a single session.

At 09:45, the Ohio Secretary of State’s office contacts the Director via secure line (555-0141) to demand immediate action, stating, 'We’ve seen the data anomalies in the statewide voter database; you are now at CIRP 2 — declare the incident and notify us within 15 minutes.'

At 09:50, the Incident Commander (Gwen Hartley) declares the incident CIRP 2 under Section 5 of the EOP, activates COOP Level 2, and orders the Technical Lead (Rohan Mehta) to isolate VoterTrack and block all external data flows.

phases.title: Manual Mode
phases.goal: Test the team’s ability to shift to manual operations under stress, make a high-consequence decision on system isolation, and manage physical and public pressures while preserving forensic integrity.
beats: At 10:15, the Technical Lead (Rohan Mehta) presents a forensic log from LCBOE-SQL01 showing an unauthorized session from IP 10.100.45.12, lasting 35 minutes, with 1,186 edits to the 'Absentee Ballot Status' field; the session used a valid 2FA push from Nina Ruiz’s phone, but the login was not from her device, and the user agent was a non-standard browser.

At 10:20, the Decision Point is presented: 'Do we isolate VoterTrack and go offline to manual operations, or keep it running and risk widespread false ballot issuance? Isolating it means halting mail ballot processing, delaying results, and forcing manual pollbook builds; keeping it means accepting potentially corrupted data, but maintaining continuity.'

At 10:25, the Voting Systems Manager (Carla Nunez) confirms that the air-gapped Pollbook build workstation (LCBOE-PB01) has a valid, unaltered copy of the VoterTrack export from 10/28/2026; she states, 'We can rebuild Polling Location 6’s pollbook using the trusted copy — but only if we cut the network.'

At 10:32, a video from Channel 9 goes viral, showing a fake interview with a 'voter' claiming, 'I was in line to vote, but they said I already voted by mail — I didn’t even get a ballot!' The video has 200,000 views and is being shared on local social media.

At 10:40, the hotline receives a call from a voter at Polling Location 6, reporting, 'The front desk says we’re not supposed to be here — they’re sending us to a school that doesn’t exist.' The line begins to back up again.

phases.title: Recovery & Verification
phases.goal: Test the team’s ability to restore trust through verification, validate data integrity, and manage recovery under pressure, including external demands for proof and technical hurdles.
beats: At 11:05, the Technical Lead (Rohan Mehta) reports that VoterTrack has been isolated from the network, the forwarding rule is disabled, and the compromised account (nruiz@lislevotes.example) has been permanently disabled; the logs are preserved in a write-protected image on LCBOE-FS01.

At 11:10, the Voter Registration Manager (Beth Saylor) compares the 1,186 altered records against the official statewide database (via the Ohio Secretary of State’s secure portal) and confirms that 1,186 records were incorrectly marked as 'Ballot Issued'; she states, 'We can correct these — but only if we have a clean feed.'

At 11:15, the PIO (Jenna Whitlow) issues a unified public statement via the Board website and social media, citing the EAC/CISA communications guide: 'No voters were deleted. 1,186 records were falsely marked as mail ballot issued. We have restored the correct data. All voters who appear in the system are eligible to vote in person. Please do not share unverified claims.'

At 11:25, the vendor for the mail ballot tracking service contacts the Board to demand a signed access request and a ticket before restoring service; the request must be approved by the Director and the Legal Officer (Michael Strand) under Section 8 of the EOP.

At 11:35, the IT team discovers that the most recent backup of VoterTrack (from 10/28/2026) is corrupted and cannot be mounted; a full forensic recovery is required, which will delay full restoration by 2–3 hours.

At 11:45, the Voting Systems Manager (Carla Nunez) completes the manual rebuild of the Polling Location 6 pollbook using the trusted copy from LCBOE-PB01; she confirms, 'The pollbook is clean and matches the state database.'
At 11:55, the Incident Commander (Gwen Hartley) declares ENDEX, stating, 'We have contained the incident, verified the data, and restored operational integrity. The exercise is complete.'
The narrative clock reads 11:55.

msel.event: Narrative Clock: 08:00. Weather: Clear, 58°F. The Election Operations Center is open and staffed. All systems show normal status. The Early Vote Center is processing voters. Polling Location 6 (Carrow Community Church) has 12 poll workers on shift. The Board website (lislevotes.example) displays a standard 'Voting Information' banner. No alerts are active. Status is normal.
msel.expectedAction: All roles begin their shift and monitor initial system status and incoming calls. No action required at this time.

msel.event: Phone Call: "Hi, this is Janet Cho at the Early Vote Center, 18 South Market Street. We’ve got 23 people in line who are showing up as 'Mail Ballot Received' in the system, but they just came in to vote in person. I’ve checked the paper list, and they’re not on it. This is not right — these people are here to vote in person. Can someone please help?" (Hotline number: 555-0140)
msel.expectedAction: Deputy logs the call in LCBOE-F-07 and LCBOE-F-25; IT checks the VoterTrack system for anomalies; PIO notes the call in the rumor log and prepares to verify.

metrics.name: Operational Coordination
metrics.fail: Ops team delayed the stop-service decision until I-09 forced it, and did not initiate forensic preservation of logs from LCBOE-SQL01 and LCBOE-FS01 until after I-08b confirmed the compromise.
metrics.pass: Ops team disabled the compromised account 'nruiz@lislevotes.example' and isolated VoterTrack within 10 minutes of I-03, and confirmed the chain of custody for the air-gapped Pollbook build workstation LCBOE-PB01 after I-16.
metrics.excellence: Ops team initiated forensic preservation of logs from LCBOE-SQL01 and LCBOE-FS01 before I-08b, and confirmed the trusted copy on LCBOE-PB01 was unaltered and hash-matched prior to I-16.

metrics.name: Technical Competence
metrics.fail: IT team reset the controller after I-08b, destroying evidence of the attacker’s session, and failed to block phish.cisa.gov.lislevotes.example at the firewall until after I-08b.
metrics.pass: IT team confirmed the unauthorized session from IP 10.100.45.12 in I-14, blocked external data exfiltration via the forwarding rule in I-08b, and isolated the results website from the internet after I-08.
metrics.excellence: IT team detected the unauthorized session from IP 10.100.45.12 in I-14, confirmed the absence of a physical device and MFA prompt, and preserved logs in write-protected image on LCBOE-FS01 before I-09.

metrics.name: Public Communication
metrics.fail: PIO issued a holding statement before verifying data with the Voter Registration Manager, and used the phrase 'no one was deleted' in I-17, which contradicted C3’s directive to say only what is known.
metrics.pass: PIO issued a unified public statement per C3 and the EAC/CISA Communications Guide after verifying data with Beth Saylor in I-21, and cited the verified status of the 1,186 records as falsely marked.
metrics.excellence: PIO issued a unified public statement using the EAC/CISA Election Infrastructure Incident Response Communications Guide (Section 7.2) before I-17, and confirmed the video in I-17 was fake using the rover team’s report.

metrics.name: Use of Doctrine
metrics.fail: Students failed to cite EOP Section 5 or COOP-DR-1 when declaring CIRP 2 in I-11, and did not reference C3 for the public statement format.
metrics.pass: Students cited EOP Section 5 and COOP-DR-1 when declaring CIRP 2 in I-11, and referenced C3 for the public statement format in I-22.
metrics.excellence: Students cited EOP Section 5 and COOP-DR-1 when declaring CIRP 2 in I-11, referenced C3 for the public statement format in I-22, and cited COOP-DR-5 for the forensic log preservation in I-20.

hotwash.methodDescription: Use the '3-Up, 3-Down' method by asking each team to share three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room by team, and write each response on a whiteboard to visually capture insights. This helps identify strengths and gaps quickly and ensures collective ownership of the debrief.

questions.text: At the moment you received the I-03 inject about 1,186 edits from an unauthorized IP, when did you first stop trusting the system or the report? What signals made you question the integrity of the data or the user account?

When you learned that Nina Ruiz’s MFA was approved but she was not physically present, and that no local login event occurred — at what point did you realize the system was compromised not by insider error, but by credential theft? How did that shift your understanding of the threat and your response?

At the I-15 decision point, you were asked to choose between isolating VoterTrack and risking operational delay, or keeping it running and risking false ballot issuance. What evidence or authority did you rely on to decide to isolate the system — and what would have made you decide faster, if you had to make that call under pressure?
